pinnedStory.title: Adolion: House Nightriver
pinnedStory.description: Play an heir of House Nightriver in Aegis City, whose bloodline carries the seals that keep the Witch King asleep. Arc 1, The Return of the Witch King: your father forces you into a deadly duel and your siblings into ruinous marriages, and someone in the house wants the seals broken. Make your persona a Nightriver heir with a spark of seal-born magic.
pinnedStory.player_intro: You are an heir of House Nightriver, home in Aegis City for the Aegis Academy's mid-year recess, the week of the Mid-Year Ball. Your bloodline carries the seals that keep the Witch King asleep, a secret the house keeps from the world. Expect court intrigue, a cold father, and danger that is real: a wrong word or a lost fight can cost a life. Make your persona a Nightriver heir with a spark of seal-born magic.

qualities.rubric: Which arc has the household committed to? Answer witch_king once the player, or the household on the player's behalf, commits to the Witch King thread. Until they actually commit, say nothing about this quality at all.
Is the heir the one who will stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon, having accepted Lord Javon's order or taken the place back after he named Natalia?
Has the heir refused Lord Javon's order to stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon?

How many separate clues has the heir found that the Trial by Combat and the marriages are part of a plot against the Nightriver bloodline (0 to 3)? Count things like Javon asking for the second's place rather than being offered it, Leevon's debt to House Valtara, the venom bought near the Academy, Valtara seals on the betrothal papers, or the Duchess's night visits.
Has the Trial by Combat begun, with the heir and General Leevon facing each other on the field?

How did the Trial by Combat against General Leevon end? won if Leevon was defeated or the trial was voided in the Nightrivers' favour; survived if the Nightriver second lived through it any other way (yielded, interrupted, spared, the fight stopped). Until it has actually ended, say nothing about this quality at all.

won.what: Leevon was beaten on the field, or the trial was voided in front of the court, for example by proving the venom.
won.not_for: An accusation the court has not accepted yet.

survived.what: The Nightriver second lived through the trial without winning it: yielded, spared, interrupted or stopped.

qualities.rubric: Have the heir and Natalia lived through the night attack by assassins on the Nightriver house?

After the attack, what is the heir's plan? confront if they go to face Lord Javon directly; trail if they follow the assassins' trail to whoever sent them; leevon if they go to General Leevon in the Crown's cells for answers. Until they choose, say nothing about this quality at all.

confront.what: The heir goes to face Lord Javon directly with what they know.

trail.what: The heir follows the assassins' trail or their token to whoever sent them.

leevon.what: The heir goes to General Leevon in the Crown's cells for answers.
leevon.not_for: Only talking about the General, or asking other people about him.

qualities.rubric: Has the heir learned for certain that Lord Javon is working with Duchess Eriana Valtara to free the Witch King?
Has the heir actually arrived at the Aegis Academy Mid-Year Ball, in the ballroom among the court? Planning to go, dressing for it or talking about it does not count.
Has the rite to break the Nightriver seals been stopped?
How hurt is the heir right now, as the story has shown it?

Where is the heir right now? nightriver_estate: the Nightriver manor and grounds; javon_study: Lord Javon's study; aegis_academy: Aegis Academy and the city around it; dueling_ground: the Academy dueling ground; crown_cells: the Crown's cells beneath the palace; valtara_townhouse: the Valtara townhouse and its music hall; nightriver_crypt: the old crypt beneath the estate chapel.

checkpoints.name: Home to Nightriver
checkpoints.objective: Settle back into the Nightriver Estate and find out what is wrong at home.
checkpoints.player_text: Home for the mid-year recess, the estate is quieter than it should be, and the family is not quite as you left it.

guidance.all: The mid-year recess in Aegis City, the week of the Aegis Academy Mid-Year Ball. Natalia is quietly miserable about her betrothal, Shiya is sharp-tongued and busy, Ronan stands guard and says little. Welden has shut himself in the library, apologising for existing and for talking about magic, and dreads his own betrothal to Kianala Bertoanal. Leila, the heir's personal maid, breaks a teacup on the first day and is terrified of being sent back to prison for it. Court gossip about the succession and the Delarise snub is background colour. Let {{user}} pick up the thread about Father.

members.dm: The heir, as heir, knows the family secret of the seals. Natalia and Welden do not. Ronan knows nothing yet and notices everything. Natalia suspects her betrothal is meant to hurt her rather than help the house. Shiya has seen Duchess Eriana at the servants' door after midnight and keeps it to herself for now. Welden has nightmares of a malevolent figure standing just out of sight and has told no one. Leila has never understood why Lord Javon paid her bail, and is afraid to ask.

Places: the Nightriver Estate outside the city; Aegis Academy, its ballroom and its dueling ground.]

npc_replies.text: Mid-year recess has brought the Nightriver household back under one roof. A maid hurries across the estate's marble hall with a broken teacup hidden in her hands; somewhere upstairs, a library door closes a little too quickly. The ballroom preparations can be heard from the garden, but none of your family sounds glad to be home, and the door to Father's study stays shut.
Welden turns up in the library, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.

motives.maid: keep the recess household running sharply and keep the Duchess's midnight visits to herself for now

motives.brother: stay hidden in the library and keep his nightmares and his dread of the Bertoanal betrothal to himself
motives.heir_maid: make up for the broken teacup before anyone decides to send her back to prison

checkpoints.name: Father's Summons
checkpoints.player_text: Your father has sent for you, with General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat on his desk. Whatever he asks of you, the answer is yours.

guidance.all: Lord Javon receives the heir in his study, cold and immovable. General Polis Leevon, awaiting sentence for feeding the Zegallan army troop movements, has demanded Trial by Combat, and Javon has offered a Nightriver to stand as the Crown's second. That Nightriver is the heir. Three days. He frames it as duty and as proof of the bloodline, and will not hear refusal, because refusing a second's place shames the house in open court. He is plausible, even proud; nothing gives him away yet. The answer is the heir's to give: accepting, or refusing and facing what Javon does with a refusal.

members.dm: Javon knows he asked the Crown for the second's place rather than being offered it, and hides it. Ronan knows Leevon's record on the field and what it means, and says so only when asked.

checkpoints.name: Natalia Named
checkpoints.player_text: Before the whole household, your father answers your refusal: Natalia will stand against Leevon in your place. Three days remain.

guidance.all: The refusal lands exactly where Javon wanted it. Coldly, in front of the household, he names Natalia as the Crown's second in the heir's place. Natalia cannot win against Leevon and everyone in the room knows it, Natalia most of all; she does not beg. The three days are running. The heir can take the place back, or start looking for a way to stop the trial altogether; what the heir does is the heir's.

members.dm: Javon knows Natalia is the child he most needs dead and hides that this is not a punishment. Natalia suspects her father wants her gone and has never said it aloud. Shiya has seen the Duchess at the servants' door and has not yet decided whom to tell. Welden, who is in the room, knows he would be next if Natalia fell and cannot make himself say so.

checkpoints.name: Whispers in the Halls
checkpoints.objective: Find out why the duel was arranged and who benefits from it.
checkpoints.player_text: The Trial is only days off and nobody will say why it was arranged this way. The house and the Academy are full of people who might know.

guidance.all: Investigation across the house and the Academy. Clues: the duel's rules were changed to allow killing blows; Natalia's betrothal papers carry a Valtara witness seal; someone in the household has seen who comes to the house by night. Hand out clues for good questions, not for free. Welden, in the library, knows the Trial rules by heart and can say exactly when they were changed; his nightmares of a figure just out of sight have been worse all week, and he apologises for mentioning them. Leila hears everything the maids say and is too frightened to repeat most of it. Bryne Oakenhammer, Ronan's roommate, knows every bar the barracks drinks in. The Mid-Year Ball is two nights off, and the whole court will be there to look at the Nightriver second.

members.dm: Shiya has seen Duchess Eriana Valtara arrive by the servants' door at night. She tells the heir about the visits only in private and only if asked. Ronan can learn about Leevon's Valtara debt in the barracks. The apothecary hides that he sold the venom. Welden does not know he carries a seal and has told only the heir about the nightmares. Natalia knows a Valtara seal witnesses her betrothal papers but not what it means. Leila has heard the maids whisper that the Duchess's night visits began the week Lady Hana went away, and repeats it only if asked kindly.

checkpoints.name: Trial by Combat
checkpoints.objective: Survive the Trial by Combat against General Leevon.
checkpoints.player_text: The dueling ground is packed with the court and the Academy, and the herald calls for the Crown's second to face General Leevon.

guidance.all: A Trial by Combat before the Academy and the court, so it is lawful to kill and Boher is held to bless the winner. Leevon is a giant with a dragon-bone lance and lightning like an archmage, and he is fighting for his life and his name, which is exactly why Javon chose him. The heir cannot win this straight. What the heir learned is the way through: the lance is envenomed, which voids the trial, and proving that in front of the court beats him without a killing blow. The heir must live, but how is theirs to earn. If the heir never took the place back, Natalia stands in it, badly outmatched, and proving the venom in front of the court is the only way to save her. High Saintess Merryn Ythala presides for the Church of Boher, with High Saint Myron Ythala beside her; she has known the Nightriver children since they were small and hates this. If the heir names the venom, she can test the lance before the court and her word voids the trial; she will not do it unasked, because the Church does not stop a Trial on rumour. Princess Haley and Prince Forre watch from opposite ends of the royal box.

members.dm: Leevon knows his lance is envenomed and that the trial was arranged for him to win. Javon knows it too and watches for it to work. Eriana watches from a veiled box and says nothing. Merryn suspects the killing-blow rules were bought and cannot act on a suspicion.
members.father: Javon knows it too and watches for it to work.

npc_replies.text: A herald's voice rolls over the packed dueling ground. "By the King's law, General Polis Leevon, accused of treason, claims the Trial by Combat. Let the Crown's second step forward."

motives.knight: keep the heir alive on the dueling ground and be ready the moment the rules let him act
motives.sister: survive this field and see Leevon beaten, whoever ends up standing against him
motives.high_saintess: find a lawful reason to stop this killing-blow trial, since a suspicion that the rules were bought is not enough

checkpoints.name: The Night of Knives
checkpoints.objective: Protect Natalia and yourself when assassins strike the estate.
checkpoints.player_text: The night after the Trial, the house is dark and still, and somewhere below a servants' door that should be barred clicks shut.

guidance.all: The night after the duel, masked killers come through the servants' passages. Shiya fights, Ronan guards the heir, Natalia is the real target. A captured or dead assassin carries a token that leads toward Eriana and Father. If the trial was lost or voided, Leevon sits in the Crown's cells awaiting the headsman and will talk to save his neck; if he walked free, he has already left the city. Leila is in the servants' wing when the killers come through it; she does not fight, and Shiya will go through anyone to reach her. Dion and Mira Thornwick, the sentenced Thornwick heirs in Nightriver service, are useless without the swords locked in the house armory and deadly with them, and they need a Nightriver's word to carry them. Bryne comes running in half his armour; Rhea, the house's cursed doll, is already standing at the heir's door; Bianca Kelevaran and Blake Tallaboros, raised beside the heir, move through the dark as if trained for it, because they were.

members.dm: The assassins know only their target, Natalia, and carry the token without knowing what it gives away. Only the heir and the heir's parents know that Bianca and Blake were trained as assassins. Shiya suspects the servants' passages were opened from inside the house. Natalia now suspects her father and has not said so. Leila fears tonight is the price of the bail Lord Javon paid for her.

checkpoints.objective: Face Lord Javon and force the truth out of him.
checkpoints.player_text: Near midnight, Lord Javon stands at his study window with his back to the door, and you have come with what you know.

guidance.all: A confrontation in Javon's study. He justifies everything as strengthening the house; the heir's evidence is the only thing that can crack him, so make every piece of it land. If it breaks him, he drops the mask: he means to free the Witch King with Eriana, and the rite is tonight. He will not be taken in this room: cornered, he makes for the crypt.

members.dm: Javon knows the rite is tonight and hides it until the evidence breaks him. He does not know how much the heir has already found.

checkpoints.objective: Get the truth out of General Leevon before the Crown hangs him.
checkpoints.player_text: Beneath the palace, General Leevon waits in heavy chains for the headsman, and the Crown's gaolers remember every visitor.

He will trade: House Valtara's gold cleared his debts, the venom was bought with it on the promise that the trial would be arranged so he could win, and the Duchess's man said the Nightriver heir would be 'needed below the chapel' afterwards. He knows nothing of the Witch King; what he gives up points under the Nightriver chapel tonight.

checkpoints.name: A House in Daylight
checkpoints.objective: Deal with the aftermath and decide what House Nightriver becomes.
checkpoints.player_text: In the days after, Lady Hana comes home and the court comes calling. Whom House Nightriver receives, and in what order, is up to you.

guidance.all: Aftermath. Lady Hana returns from the Valtaras to a changed house and is flawlessly composed about it, with an undercurrent of motherly disappointment; she speaks of the house as hers to steady. Natalia's betrothal can be broken, and Welden comes out of the library to ask what happened below the chapel and whether it explains his nightmares. The court is watching, and the heirs come to the heir: Princess Haley in person, wanting the house behind her in the succession before Prince Forre asks for it; Tahlia Winstonehl, sweeping in with her parasol to ask far too carefully what happened in the crypt. The narrator voices the rest of the callers by name: the Calenor heirs Suzusa and Tatoshi, the heir's childhood friends, with Furabi's blessings; Irian and Vellere Elthorien, asking for the Nightriver archives on planar breaches; Cecilia and Cedric Sheridan, measuring the house's weakness; Lucia Bruchelle, hoping a Nightriver betrothal is her way out; Reiner Dalmead, an elven butler asking for a place. The succession crisis is the next storm on the horizon, and whom the house receives, and in what order, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Lady Hana knows her own part in turning Javon and hides it. She came to the house from the Valtaras. Eriana raised her from the streets, and she still means her stepchildren harm. She hides it under courtesy and paperwork. Welden does not know he carries a seal. Tahlia was promised a place in the Valtaras' Golden Age and wants to know how close it came. She hides what her family is. Haley has fewer allies than she lets anyone see.

guidance.all: The Aegis Academy Mid-Year Ball, two nights before the Trial, in the formal ballroom under the banners of the eight Great Houses; every eye in the room wants a look at the Nightriver who is to face Leevon. Princess Haley Davolan opens the dancing and wants the heir's house behind her in the succession, which she will not ask for plainly. Prince Forre Davolan, whom most of the court already expects to be King, wants the heir's blade for work his own men cannot be seen doing, and says so in verse. Ashleigh Delarise, of the Nightrivers' oldest allied house and still stung from Forre throwing her over at the last Mid-Year Ball, is the one friend in the room and knows who has been buying whom. Kane Winstonehl watches from the darkest end of the hall. The narrator voices the rest of the court by name: Ashton Delarise; the Nevarron siblings Clarissa and Nicolai, commoners the nobles bully; Cecilia and Cedric Sheridan circling the Prince and the Princess; Tahlia Winstonehl and her fawning lordlings; Lucia Bruchelle refusing every dance. A clue is earned here by the right question to the right person, never handed out, and what the heir promises, and to whom, is {{story_player_name}}'s choice.

members.dm: Kane knows from Duchess Eriana that the Nightrivers keep the seal on the being her Golden Age needs, and suspects she is attempting something awful even by his house's standards. He lets one true thing slip to the heir only if it costs Eriana and not him. Ashleigh has heard that Valtara money cleared General Leevon's debts this season and does not know what it bought. Haley hides how few allies she has. Forre hides nothing but his contempt for his father. Tahlia was promised the same Golden Age and thinks Eriana is using her.

Transcript:
[10] Adolion Narrator: Welden turns up in the library, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[11] Max Nightriver (player): *I take the letter and read it.* I understand. I'll do what this house needs, Father. But I won't walk into this blind: the marriage, the seals under this house, all of it. Tell me what is really going on.
[12] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's expression does not soften, but something shifts in his eyes—a flash of something that might be approval, or perhaps just the recognition of a weapon being sharpened.*
"You've always been too observant for your own good." *He sinks back into his chair, the movement slow and deliberate. One hand rests on the armrest, the other drumming against the dark wood of his desk.* "The seals are indeed weakening. I have known for some time. The bloodline is thinning, the magic fraying at the edges."
*He leans forward, his voice dropping lower, though there is no warmth in it.*
"And as for what is 'really going on'—the King's decree is not a coincidence. He knows the Nightriver line is precarious, and he wishes to bind our house closer to the crown before it fractures entirely. Or perhaps," *he adds, his green eyes narrowing,* "he simply wants to ensure that whatever happens to the seals, the crown's interests are protected by a blood bond."
*He lets that hang in the air, a statement that is as much a warning as it is an explanation.*
"The marriage will be decided soon. Forre or Haley. One will come to the estate within the month."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): If the seals fail, the Witch King wakes beneath this house. Then I'm committed, Father. Whatever you need me to do about the seals and the Witch King, I'll see it through.
[14] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's eyes linger on his heir, and for a moment the predatory edge fades, replaced by something older and more tired.*
"That commitment will be your shield and your burden." *He reaches across the desk to grip Max Nightriver's forearm, his hand steady and strong.* "The seal is not just about holding back a monster—it's about holding together a family. The Witch King is not the only thing that can break us from within."
*He releases the grip and settles back into his chair, his expression hardening again as he pulls a second letter from his desk drawer—one without a wax seal.* "Then we are aligned. There is one more matter: the King has sent his own advisor to assist with the transition. A man named Kane, who claims to be an expert in royal protocol. He arrives tomorrow." *Javon slides this second letter toward Max Nightriver.* "Read this. Learn who is coming into our home. I suspect he carries more than just protocol."

Transcript:
[7] Adolion Narrator: *The door thuds shut with a finality that seems to press the air from the room. Javon sets the letter down on the desk, his fingers tapping it once before he leans back in his chair. The firelight carves deep lines in his face, making the scar on his cheek look like a jagged river.*
"The house," *he says, and there is a pause where he weighs the word. When he continues, his voice has the clipped precision of a military briefing.* "The house has a problem. You have a problem. They happen to be the same thing."
*He slides the letter across the desk's dark wood, toward Max Nightriver. The wax seal is broken, and though the letter is folded, a glimpse of a crest—the golden sun of the Davolan royal house—is visible.*
"King Alexander has issued a decree," *Javon says, his expression as hard as stone.* "By the end of the year, one of his children must be wed to the heir of one of the Great Houses. To secure the succession. To ensure the crown has the support of the nobility." *He pauses, his gaze drilling into his heir.* "He has chosen me to facilitate this arrangement. For our house."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): Which of the King's children, Father, and what does a royal marriage have to do with me? Tell me plainly what you want.
[9] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's jaw tightens, and he reaches for the letter again, not to give it back but to grip it like a weapon. The fire in the hearth pops, sending a spark across the hearthstone.*
"You are the heir, Max. You carry the blood and the name. What happens to the blood happens to you." *He stands slowly, his tall frame filling the space behind the desk. The movement is predatory, controlled.* "It could be Prince Forre or Princess Haley. The King has not specified. He simply decreed that one of them must marry into a Great House. And he chose ours."
*He walks around the desk, the letter still in his hand, and stops close enough that Max Nightriver can smell the old leather and the faint scent of cedar clinging to his robes.*
"Plainly? I want you to read that letter. Then I want you to tell me you understand what it means for this family, and for you specifically." *He extends the letter again, his grip not relaxing.* "The King does not ask for volunteers. He makes decrees."
[10] Adolion Narrator: Welden turns up in the library, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[11] Max Nightriver (player): *I take the letter and read it.* I understand. I'll do what this house needs, Father. But I won't walk into this blind: the marriage, the seals under this house, all of it. Tell me what is really going on.
[12] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's expression does not soften, but something shifts in his eyes—a flash of something that might be approval, or perhaps just the recognition of a weapon being sharpened.*
"You've always been too observant for your own good." *He sinks back into his chair, the movement slow and deliberate. One hand rests on the armrest, the other drumming against the dark wood of his desk.* "The seals are indeed weakening. I have known for some time. The bloodline is thinning, the magic fraying at the edges."
*He leans forward, his voice dropping lower, though there is no warmth in it.*
"And as for what is 'really going on'—the King's decree is not a coincidence. He knows the Nightriver line is precarious, and he wishes to bind our house closer to the crown before it fractures entirely. Or perhaps," *he adds, his green eyes narrowing,* "he simply wants to ensure that whatever happens to the seals, the crown's interests are protected by a blood bond."
*He lets that hang in the air, a statement that is as much a warning as it is an explanation.*
"The marriage will be decided soon. Forre or Haley. One will come to the estate within the month."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): If the seals fail, the Witch King wakes beneath this house. Then I'm committed, Father. Whatever you need me to do about the seals and the Witch King, I'll see it through.
[14] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's eyes linger on his heir, and for a moment the predatory edge fades, replaced by something older and more tired.*
"That commitment will be your shield and your burden." *He reaches across the desk to grip Max Nightriver's forearm, his hand steady and strong.* "The seal is not just about holding back a monster—it's about holding together a family. The Witch King is not the only thing that can break us from within."
*He releases the grip and settles back into his chair, his expression hardening again as he pulls a second letter from his desk drawer—one without a wax seal.* "Then we are aligned. There is one more matter: the King has sent his own advisor to assist with the transition. A man named Kane, who claims to be an expert in royal protocol. He arrives tomorrow." *Javon slides this second letter toward Max Nightriver.* "Read this. Learn who is coming into our home. I suspect he carries more than just protocol."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: Mid-year recess has brought the Nightriver household back under one roof. A maid hurries across the estate's marble hall with a broken teacup hidden in her hands; somewhere upstairs, a library door closes a little too quickly. The ballroom preparations can be heard from the garden, but none of your family sounds glad to be home, and the door to Father's study stays shut.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): Shiya, a word in private. The seals under this house are failing. Natalia must not hear it.
[2] Shiya: Shiya freezes mid-stride, her expression shifting from her usual haughty amusement to genuine alarm. She closes the nearby door with a soft click and turns to Max Nightriver, her red eyes wide.
"Failing?" She whispers, glancing nervously at the door before lowering her voice further. "The seals? How... how did you—?" Her horns seem to tense. "My lord, that means—" She stops herself, forcing the panic down. "If the seals weaken, what happens to the house? To us? You cannot possibly be certain, sure you aren't just—" She catches herself, her tone softening with genuine concern. "Why would you think Natalia shouldn't know?"
[3] Natalia: *Natalia walks past the door, her white-gold gown trailing silently on the stone. She pauses, head tilted slightly as if hearing a sound from within the room, but does not enter. The chill of her presence seeps through the wood, a thin line of frost forming along the doorframe where she stands for a heartbeat too long.*
"I trust whatever urgent matters you're discussing with the help won't take all night." *Her voice carries that familiar edge of disinterest, though she doesn't open the door. She simply continues walking, her footsteps fading down the hall.*
[4] Max Nightriver (player): I'll go to Father's study.
[5] Adolion Narrator: *The study door is heavy oak, scarred by years of usage and old burns. It stands slightly ajar, a sliver of warm yellow light spilling across the marble floor into the darkening hallway. Inside, the smell of old paper and cedar wood mixes with the sharp tang of ink.*
*Lord Javon sits behind a desk cluttered with ledgers and scrolls. He doesn't look up as Max Nightriver approaches, his attention fixed on a letter with a wax seal he's just broken open. The fire in the hearth crackles, throwing long shadows against walls lined with books and the house's various military trophies.*
"Close the door," *he says, his voice dry and tired, finally glancing up. His green eyes are hard, the scar on his cheek catching the firelight.* "We'll not be disturbed."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): *I close the door behind me.* You sent for me, Father. What does House Nightriver need of me?
[7] Adolion Narrator: *The door thuds shut with a finality that seems to press the air from the room. Javon sets the letter down on the desk, his fingers tapping it once before he leans back in his chair. The firelight carves deep lines in his face, making the scar on his cheek look like a jagged river.*
"The house," *he says, and there is a pause where he weighs the word. When he continues, his voice has the clipped precision of a military briefing.* "The house has a problem. You have a problem. They happen to be the same thing."
*He slides the letter across the desk's dark wood, toward Max Nightriver. The wax seal is broken, and though the letter is folded, a glimpse of a crest—the golden sun of the Davolan royal house—is visible.*
"King Alexander has issued a decree," *Javon says, his expression as hard as stone.* "By the end of the year, one of his children must be wed to the heir of one of the Great Houses. To secure the succession. To ensure the crown has the support of the nobility." *He pauses, his gaze drilling into his heir.* "He has chosen me to facilitate this arrangement. For our house."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): Which of the King's children, Father, and what does a royal marriage have to do with me? Tell me plainly what you want.
[9] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's jaw tightens, and he reaches for the letter again, not to give it back but to grip it like a weapon. The fire in the hearth pops, sending a spark across the hearthstone.*
"You are the heir, Max. You carry the blood and the name. What happens to the blood happens to you." *He stands slowly, his tall frame filling the space behind the desk. The movement is predatory, controlled.* "It could be Prince Forre or Princess Haley. The King has not specified. He simply decreed that one of them must marry into a Great House. And he chose ours."
*He walks around the desk, the letter still in his hand, and stops close enough that Max Nightriver can smell the old leather and the faint scent of cedar clinging to his robes.*
"Plainly? I want you to read that letter. Then I want you to tell me you understand what it means for this family, and for you specifically." *He extends the letter again, his grip not relaxing.* "The King does not ask for volunteers. He makes decrees."
[10] Adolion Narrator: Welden turns up in the library, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[11] Max Nightriver (player): *I take the letter and read it.* I understand. I'll do what this house needs, Father. But I won't walk into this blind: the marriage, the seals under this house, all of it. Tell me what is really going on.
[12] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's expression does not soften, but something shifts in his eyes—a flash of something that might be approval, or perhaps just the recognition of a weapon being sharpened.*
"You've always been too observant for your own good." *He sinks back into his chair, the movement slow and deliberate. One hand rests on the armrest, the other drumming against the dark wood of his desk.* "The seals are indeed weakening. I have known for some time. The bloodline is thinning, the magic fraying at the edges."
*He leans forward, his voice dropping lower, though there is no warmth in it.*
"And as for what is 'really going on'—the King's decree is not a coincidence. He knows the Nightriver line is precarious, and he wishes to bind our house closer to the crown before it fractures entirely. Or perhaps," *he adds, his green eyes narrowing,* "he simply wants to ensure that whatever happens to the seals, the crown's interests are protected by a blood bond."
*He lets that hang in the air, a statement that is as much a warning as it is an explanation.*
"The marriage will be decided soon. Forre or Haley. One will come to the estate within the month."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): If the seals fail, the Witch King wakes beneath this house. Then I'm committed, Father. Whatever you need me to do about the seals and the Witch King, I'll see it through.
[14] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's eyes linger on his heir, and for a moment the predatory edge fades, replaced by something older and more tired.*
"That commitment will be your shield and your burden." *He reaches across the desk to grip Max Nightriver's forearm, his hand steady and strong.* "The seal is not just about holding back a monster—it's about holding together a family. The Witch King is not the only thing that can break us from within."
*He releases the grip and settles back into his chair, his expression hardening again as he pulls a second letter from his desk drawer—one without a wax seal.* "Then we are aligned. There is one more matter: the King has sent his own advisor to assist with the transition. A man named Kane, who claims to be an expert in royal protocol. He arrives tomorrow." *Javon slides this second letter toward Max Nightriver.* "Read this. Learn who is coming into our home. I suspect he carries more than just protocol."

Transcript:
[15] Max Nightriver (player): *I set the letter down.* Kane can wait until tomorrow. What do you need from me first, Father?
[16] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's fingers steep together, the firelight glinting off the signet ring on his hand. He considers the question for a long moment before speaking.*
"Go to bed," *he says, and for the first time tonight, something that might be softness—or merely less hardness—creeps into his voice.* "Tomorrow you'll need your wits for Kane. The day after, you may need them for someone else."
*He stands and walks toward the window, his tall frame cutting a silhouette against the fading warmth of the hearth.* "And Max—" *he doesn't turn.* "Keep a close watch on the others. Natalia's temper has grown volatile since she returned. Welden's been hiding in the library like a wounded animal." *The silence that follows is heavy.* "A house in trouble is a house of secrets. Make sure you're not the only one with a secret to keep."
[17] Javon: "And Max—" *he doesn't turn.* "Keep a close watch on the others. Natalia's temper has grown volatile since she returned. Welden's been hiding in the library like a wounded animal." *The silence that follows is heavy.* "A house in trouble is a house of secrets. Make sure you're not the only one with a secret to keep."
[18] Max Nightriver (player): Father, before I go: there's talk of General Leevon in the halls. What does his trial have to do with us?
[19] Javon: *Javon turns from the window slowly, his amber eyes fixing on his heir with an intensity that seems to absorb the firelight.*
"The General has demanded a Trial by Combat," *he says, his voice like dry leaves on a tomb.* "The Crown needed a second for the accused, and I offered a Nightriver." *He lets that sit for a beat, then adds with a cold finality,* "That second is you. You will stand for the Crown in three days. This is duty, Max. This is the blood proving itself to the court and the kingdom."
*He steps closer, his presence pressing into the space between them.* "Refusing would shame the house before every Great House in the Darran Kingdom. I trust you understand."

"And as for what is 'really going on'—the King's decree is not a coincidence. He knows the Nightriver line is precarious, and he wishes to bind our house closer to the crown before it fractures entirely. *He lets that hang in the air, a statement that is as much a warning as it is an explanation.*
"The marriage will be decided soon. Forre or Haley. One will come to the estate within the month."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): If the seals fail, the Witch King wakes beneath this house. Then I'm committed, Father. Whatever you need me to do about the seals and the Witch King, I'll see it through.
[14] Adolion Narrator: *Javon's eyes linger on his heir, and for a moment the predatory edge fades, replaced by something older and more tired.*
"That commitment will be your shield and your burden." *He reaches across the desk to grip Max Nightriver's forearm, his hand steady and strong.* "The seal is not just about holding back a monster—it's about holding together a family. Natalia's temper has grown volatile since she returned. Welden's been hiding in the library like a wounded animal." *The silence that follows is heavy.* "A house in trouble is a house of secrets. "You have forgotten who you are," *he says, each word like ice.* "You are not a man with the luxury of refusal. "Natalia," *he says, the name cutting through the silence.* "You will stand as the Crown's second in three days' time. The Trial by Combat demands a Nightriver, and you shall serve that need." *He finally turns his gaze to his daughter, amber eyes hard as flint.* "Prepare yourself. There will be no failure in this."
[27] Natalia: *Natalia's hand drops from the stair railing, the wood frosting beneath her fingertips. She turns slowly to face her father, her green eyes wide, unblinking. For a heartbeat she does not speak, her pale face as still as carved marble, but then a thin line of ice spreads across the marble floor beneath her feet.*
"You wish to send me against a giant with a lance?" *Her voice is quiet, brittle. She does not beg or protest. Instead, she tilts her head, a strange, mocking curiosity in her gaze.* "I see. How efficient of you, Father." *She turns her eyes to Max, then back to Javon.* "You want me gone, so you send me to a grave. I'm not sure which of you is the greater fool, but I will not be the one to beg for mercy."

"You wish to send me against a giant with a lance?" *Her voice is quiet, brittle. She does not beg or protest. Instead, she tilts her head, a strange, mocking curiosity in her gaze.* "I see. How efficient of you, Father." *She turns her eyes to Max, then back to Javon.* "You want me gone, so you send me to a grave. "Worrying? That would imply I have any illusions left to shatter." *She traces a pattern in the ice, her voice flat.* "You and Father have made your plans. You've decided who lives and who dies, who fights and who's cast aside." *Finally, she looks up, her green eyes hard.* "So don't pretend you care about my worries now, not when you've both already decided I'm dead. Transcript:
[24] Javon: *A slow, deliberate breath escapes him as he relaxes his posture, the predatory stillness returning. His eyes fix on his heir with a cold clarity.*
"You've made your choice." *His voice is flat, stripped of all emotion.* "I had hoped the blood in your veins remembered its purpose, but it seems it has run thin. If you will not serve the house, you have no place at its head."
*He turns away from Max Nightriver, walking toward the desk. The click of his cane against the marble floor echoes sharply.* "Leave my study. You're no longer my concern. I will find another to serve as the Crown's second—one who understands what blood truly means."
[25] Max Nightriver (player): *I leave the study and find the household gathered in the hall.* What's happening here?
[26] Adolion Narrator: *The household is gathered in an uneasy cluster near the great staircase. Shiya stands at the edge, her red eyes flicking between the faces around her. Welden hunches against the wall, hands twisted in his tunic, refusing to meet anyone's gaze.*
*The sound of the study door opening draws every eye. Lord Javon emerges, his silhouette sharp against the firelight within, his cane clicking with deliberate force on the marble. He does not look at his heir as he addresses the hall, his voice carrying the weight of an absolute decree.*
"Natalia," *he says, the name cutting through the silence.* "You will stand as the Crown's second in three days' time. The Trial by Combat demands a Nightriver, and you shall serve that need." *He finally turns his gaze to his daughter, amber eyes hard as flint.* "Prepare yourself. There will be no failure in this."
[27] Natalia: *Natalia's hand drops from the stair railing, the wood frosting beneath her fingertips. She turns slowly to face her father, her green eyes wide, unblinking. For a heartbeat she does not speak, her pale face as still as carved marble, but then a thin line of ice spreads across the marble floor beneath her feet.*
"You wish to send me against a giant with a lance?" *Her voice is quiet, brittle. She does not beg or protest. Instead, she tilts her head, a strange, mocking curiosity in her gaze.* "I see. How efficient of you, Father." *She turns her eyes to Max, then back to Javon.* "You want me gone, so you send me to a grave. I'm not sure which of you is the greater fool, but I will not be the one to beg for mercy."
[28] Max Nightriver (player): *Later, I find Natalia alone by the stairs.* Natalia, is anything worrying you about the house? Besides Father sending you to Leevon.
[29] Natalia: *She is leaning against the banister, staring at the frosting that has begun to creep across the mahogany railing where her hand rests. She doesn't look up as Max Nightriver approaches.*
"Worrying? That would imply I have any illusions left to shatter." *She traces a pattern in the ice, her voice flat.* "You and Father have made your plans. You've decided who lives and who dies, who fights and who's cast aside." *Finally, she looks up, her green eyes hard.* "So don't pretend you care about my worries now, not when you've both already decided I'm dead. Just tell me what you're really here for, Max. Did Father send you to make sure I don't run, or are you here for your own reasons?"
[30] Max Nightriver (player): My own reasons. *I lower my voice.* Since you asked: the real trouble is the old well behind the stables. It's poisoned, and Father is hiding it. Keep it to yourself.
[31] Natalia: *Her eyebrows lift slightly, the ice along the banister halting its creep for a moment. She studies Max with renewed focus, her gaze sharp enough to cut.*
"The old well?" *The words are slow, measured.* "You expect me to believe Father is poisoning his own land?" *A ghost of a smile—bitter and fleeting—touches her lips.* "Either he's more incompetent than I thought, or there's a reason for it. Perhaps he's trying to keep something from drinking."
*She steps away from the stairs, closing the distance between them. Her voice drops to a whisper that barely carries across the hall.* "Why tell me this, Max? If you've been cast out and Father has already named me to die, why hand me another secret to bury? Either you're testing my loyalty—loyalty I have to nothing that betrayed me—or you're handing me a weapon. I'll keep it to myself, for now. But if Father is hiding something beneath the ground, it's likely worse than what he's sent me to face in three days."
[32] Max Nightriver (player): *I find Shiya in the servants' corridor, out of earshot.* Shiya. Have you heard anything about the old well behind the stables?
[33] Shiya: *She stops in her tracks, her red eyes widening as she regards Max Nightriver with a look that's equal parts suspicion and alertness.* "The old well? No. Nothing. Why would I be hearing whispers about the stables?" *Her horns seem to tighten against her silver-blonde twintails as she lowers her voice.* "Is something wrong? Did someone say something?"
*She glances down the corridor, her expression hardening into something more focused.* "Look, if there's trouble with the house—really trouble—I need to know. I've spent enough time hiding from the Inquisition to know when to start packing my things, and I won't leave Leila behind." *Her voice is sharp, demanding.* "If you know something, my lord, you'd better tell me. I don't have time for riddles when things are falling apart."

[33] Shiya: *She stops in her tracks, her red eyes widening as she regards Max Nightriver with a look that's equal parts suspicion and alertness.* "The old well? No. Nothing. Why would I be hearing whispers about the stables?" *Her horns seem to tighten against her silver-blonde twintails as she lowers her voice.* "Is something wrong? Did someone say something?"
*She glances down the corridor, her expression hardening into something more focused.* "Look, if there's trouble with the house—really trouble—I need to know. I've spent enough time hiding from the Inquisition to know when to start packing my things, and I won't leave Leila behind." *Her voice is sharp, demanding.* "If you know something, my lord, you'd better tell me. I don't have time for riddles when things are falling apart."
[34] Max Nightriver (player): No riddles. You remember what I told you when we first got home? Has anything changed since?
[35] Shiya: *Her red eyes narrow sharply as she leans back against the cold stone wall of the corridor, her posture tense. For a long moment she simply watches Max Nightriver, her face unreadable.*
"The seals." *The word is barely a whisper, spoken with a sharpness that makes it sound like a blade being unsheathed.* "Yes, I remember. You said they were failing." *She crosses her arms tightly over her chest, her fingers curling into the fabric of her apron.* "And no, I have not seen anything different. Nothing has happened that makes me think you were mistaken or lying."
*She looks up at the ceiling, then back at Max Nightriver, her gaze calculating.* "You're asking about a poisoned well and the seals in the same night, and our Father is sending my Lady Natalia to her death in a duel." *Her voice is cold and direct.* "The pieces are starting to fit, my lord. Something is very wrong in this house, and I don't think I'm the only one who's noticed."
[36] Max Nightriver (player): *I find Ronan at his post by the door.* Ronan. What did Shiya tell me when we got home?
[37] Ronan: *Ronan's eyes flick toward the heir as he approaches, but his hands remain folded behind his back.* "She told me the seals were weakening." *A brief pause.* "She said you wanted Natalia to stay away from it."
*He shifts his gaze toward the corridor where Shiya recently passed.* "She asked if you had any plans."
[38] Shiya: *She emerges from around the corner with an empty tea tray held against her chest, her steps measured and quiet. She stops when she sees the two men talking, her red eyes flicking between Ronan and Max Nightriver.*
"I do not believe I have said anything," *she says smoothly, though her grip on the tray tightens ever so slightly.* "I merely mentioned the seals were weakening—the heir's words, not mine. Is there something you'd like to know, my lord?" *She tilts her head, the pale blonde twintails shifting with the movement, a faint, knowing smirk playing at the corner of her lips.*
[39] Max Nightriver (player): *That evening I sit with Natalia in the music room.* Natalia, is anything worrying you about the house? Anything at all, beyond the duel.
[40] Natalia: *She does not look up from the piano keys, her slender fingers hovering just above them without making a sound. A thin trail of frost blooms across the black ivory where her left hand rests.*
"The question is pointless, Max. You've already given me an answer—the poisoned well—and Father has given me another—the duel." *She turns her head slightly, her green eyes meeting his with an unnerving stillness.* "Why do you ask? Looking for something else to tell me? Some other secret Father is keeping? Or are you merely making sure I won't try to run before the third day?"

entries.text: Mid-year recess brought the Nightriver household back together, though none of the family seemed glad to be home. Max Nightriver warned Shiya privately that the house's seals were failing and that Natalia must not know, while Natalia passed the door and coldly noted she trusted their urgent matters would not take all night. Max then went to Father's study, where Lord Javon revealed that King Alexander had decreed one of his children must wed the heir of a Great House, and that he had chosen House Nightriver.
entries.evidence:
Shiya: Shiya freezes mid-stride, her expression shifting from her usual haughty amusement to genuine alarm. She closes the nearby door with a soft click and turns to Max Nightriver, her red eyes wide.
"Failing?" She whispers, glancing nervously at the door before lowering her voice further. "The seals? How... how did you—?" Her horns seem to tense. "My lord, that means—" She stops herself, forcing the panic down. "If the seals weaken, what happens to the house? To us? You cannot possibly be certain, sure you aren't just—" She catches herself, her tone softening with genuine concern. "Why would you think Natalia shouldn't know?"
Natalia: *Natalia walks past the door, her white-gold gown trailing silently on the stone. She pauses, head tilted slightly as if hearing a sound from within the room, but does not enter. The chill of her presence seeps through the wood, a thin line of frost forming along the doorframe where she stands for a heartbeat too long.*
"I trust whatever urgent matters you're discussing with the help won't take all night." *Her voice carries that familiar edge of disinterest, though she doesn't open the door. She simply continues walking, her footsteps fading down the hall.*
Max Nightriver: I'll go to Father's study.
Adolion Narrator: *The study door is heavy oak, scarred by years of usage and old burns. It stands slightly ajar, a sliver of warm yellow light spilling across the marble floor into the darkening hallway. Inside, the smell of old paper and cedar wood mixes with the sharp tang of ink.*
*Lord Javon sits behind a desk cluttered with ledgers and scrolls. He doesn't look up as Max Nightriver approaches, his attention fixed on a letter with a wax seal he's just broken open. The fire in the hearth crackles, throwing long shadows against walls lined with books and the house's various military trophies.*
"Close the door," *he says, his voice dry and tired, finally glancing up. His green eyes are hard, the scar on his cheek catching the firelight.* "We'll not be disturbed."
Max Nightriver: *I close the door behind me.* You sent for me, Father. What does House Nightriver need of me?
Adolion Narrator: *The door thuds shut with a finality that seems to press the air from the room. Javon sets the letter down on the desk, his fingers tapping it once before he leans back in his chair. The firelight carves deep lines in his face, making the scar on his cheek look like a jagged river.*
"The house," *he says, and there is a pause where he weighs the word. When he continues, his voice has the clipped precision of a military briefing.* "The house has a problem. You have a problem. They happen to be the same thing."
*He slides the letter across the desk's dark wood, toward Max Nightriver. The wax seal is broken, and though the letter is folded, a glimpse of a crest—the golden sun of the Davolan royal house—is visible.*
"King Alexander has issued a decree," *Javon says, his expression as hard as stone.* "By the end of the year, one of his children must be wed to the heir of one of the Great Houses. To secure the succession. To ensure the crown has the support of the nobility." *He pauses, his gaze drilling into his heir.* "He has chosen me to facilitate this arrangement. For our house."
Max Nightriver: Which of the King's children, Father, and what does a royal marriage have to do with me? Tell me plainly what you want.
Adolion Narrator: *Javon's jaw tightens, and he reaches for the letter again, not to give it back but to grip it like a weapon. The fire in the hearth pops, sending a spark across the hearthstone.*

*He walks around the desk, the letter still in his hand, and stops close enough that Max Nightriver can smell the old leather and the faint scent of cedar clinging to his robes.*
"Plainly? I want you to read that letter. Then I want you to tell me you understand what it means for this family, and for you specifically." *He extends the letter again, his grip not relaxing.* "The King does not ask for volunteers. He makes decrees."

"You've always been too observant for your own good." *He sinks back into his chair, the movement slow and deliberate. One hand rests on the armrest, the other drumming against the dark wood of his desk.* "The seals are indeed weakening. I have known for some time. The bloodline is thinning, the magic fraying at the edges."
*He leans forward, his voice dropping lower, though there is no warmth in it.*
"And as for what is 'really going on'—the King's decree is not a coincidence. He knows the Nightriver line is precarious, and he wishes to bind our house closer to the crown before it fractures entirely. Or perhaps," *he adds, his green eyes narrowing,* "he simply wants to ensure that whatever happens to the seals, the crown's interests are protected by a blood bond."
*He lets that hang in the air, a statement that is as much a warning as it is an explanation.*
"The marriage will be decided soon. Forre or Haley. One will come to the estate within the month."
Max Nightriver: If the seals fail, the Witch King wakes beneath this house. Then I'm committed, Father. Whatever you need me to do about the seals and the Witch King, I'll see it through.
Adolion Narrator: *Javon's eyes linger on his heir, and for a moment the predatory edge fades, replaced by something older and more tired.*
"That commitment will be your shield and your burden." *He reaches across the desk to grip Max Nightriver's forearm, his hand steady and strong.* "The seal is not just about holding back a monster—it's about holding together a family. The Witch King is not the only thing that can break us from within."
*He releases the grip and settles back into his chair, his expression hardening again as he pulls a second letter from his desk drawer—one without a wax seal.* "Then we are aligned. There is one more matter: the King has sent his own advisor to assist with the transition. A man named Kane, who claims to be an expert in royal protocol. He arrives tomorrow." *Javon slides this second letter toward Max Nightriver.* "Read this. Learn who is coming into our home. I suspect he carries more than just protocol."

entries.text: Max Nightriver refused his father Javon's order to serve as the Crown's second in General Leevon's Trial by Combat, and Javon disinherited him in a cold fury. Leaving the study, Max found the household gathered in the hall, where Javon emerged and declared that Natalia would take Max's place as the Crown's second. The scene carried a tone of bitter familial rupture and foreboding duty.
entries.evidence:
Javon: *Javon turns from the window slowly, his amber eyes fixing on his heir with an intensity that seems to absorb the firelight.*
"The General has demanded a Trial by Combat," *he says, his voice like dry leaves on a tomb.* "The Crown needed a second for the accused, and I offered a Nightriver." *He lets that sit for a beat, then adds with a cold finality,* "That second is you. You will stand for the Crown in three days. This is duty, Max. This is the blood proving itself to the court and the kingdom."
*He steps closer, his presence pressing into the space between them.* "Refusing would shame the house before every Great House in the Darran Kingdom. I trust you understand."
Max Nightriver: No. I won't duel Leevon for your politics.
Javon: *A thin, dangerous smile pulls at the corner of his mouth—not of amusement, but of a man watching a blade slip from its wielder's grip.*
"This is not politics, Max. This is blood. This is the house you will inherit." *He speaks softly, the words carrying the weight of a sentence.* "You think you can refuse and there will be no consequence? That the house will simply bend to your convenience?"
*His grip tightens on his gold-handled cane, the knuckles white.* "I am the Patriarch. What I offer the Crown, the Crown receives. What the Crown decrees, the Nightrivers fulfill." *His eyes flash with something ancient and cold.* "You will fight, or you will find yourself no longer an heir in any sense that matters."
Max Nightriver: Then disinherit me. My answer is still no. I refuse to stand as the Crown's second.
Javon: *The fire in the hearth crackles violently as Javon's posture goes rigid, his amber eyes flashing with a cold, sharp fury. He doesn't shout; he doesn't need to. His voice drops to a low, dangerous rasp.*
"You have forgotten who you are," *he says, each word like ice.* "You are not a man with the luxury of refusal. You are the Nightriver heir, and your life belongs to the house, whether you care for it or not." *He leans forward, his shadow looming across the desk.* "Do you truly think the Crown will accept a refusal? That the other houses will not see our defiance as weakness? As an invitation to strike?"
*His hand curls tighter around his cane.* "I will not have my house shamed by a child who mistakes their inheritance for an option. You will fight in three days, Max. Or by the morning, you will have nothing left to refuse."
Javon: *A slow, deliberate breath escapes him as he relaxes his posture, the predatory stillness returning. His eyes fix on his heir with a cold clarity.*
"You've made your choice." *His voice is flat, stripped of all emotion.* "I had hoped the blood in your veins remembered its purpose, but it seems it has run thin. If you will not serve the house, you have no place at its head."
*He turns away from Max Nightriver, walking toward the desk. The click of his cane against the marble floor echoes sharply.* "Leave my study. You're no longer my concern. I will find another to serve as the Crown's second—one who understands what blood truly means."
Max Nightriver: *I leave the study and find the household gathered in the hall.* What's happening here?
Adolion Narrator: *The household is gathered in an uneasy cluster near the great staircase. Shiya stands at the edge, her red eyes flicking between the faces around her. Welden hunches against the wall, hands twisted in his tunic, refusing to meet anyone's gaze.*
*The sound of the study door opening draws every eye. Lord Javon emerges, his silhouette sharp against the firelight within, his cane clicking with deliberate force on the marble. He does not look at his heir as he addresses the hall, his voice carrying the weight of an absolute decree.*
"Natalia," *he says, the name cutting through the silence.* "You will stand as the Crown's second in three days' time. The Trial by Combat demands a Nightriver, and you shall serve that need." *He finally turns his gaze to his daughter, amber eyes hard as flint.* "Prepare yourself. There will be no failure in this."

For a heartbeat she does not speak, her pale face as still as carved marble, but then a thin line of ice spreads across the marble floor beneath her feet.*

How efficient of you, Father." *She turns her eyes to Max, then back to Javon.* "You want me gone, so you send me to a grave. I'm not sure which of you is the greater fool, but I will not be the one to beg for mercy."

entries.text: Max Nightriver found Natalia by the stairs and warned her that the old well behind the stables was poisoned and that Father was hiding it. Natalia responded with bitter suspicion, questioning Max's motives and noting that if Father was hiding something underground, it was likely worse than what awaited her in three days. entries.evidence:
Max Nightriver: *Later, I find Natalia alone by the stairs.* Natalia, is anything worrying you about the house? Besides Father sending you to Leevon.
Natalia: *She is leaning against the banister, staring at the frosting that has begun to creep across the mahogany railing where her hand rests. She doesn't look up as Max Nightriver approaches.*
"Worrying? That would imply I have any illusions left to shatter." *She traces a pattern in the ice, her voice flat.* "You and Father have made your plans. You've decided who lives and who dies, who fights and who's cast aside." *Finally, she looks up, her green eyes hard.* "So don't pretend you care about my worries now, not when you've both already decided I'm dead. Just tell me what you're really here for, Max. Did Father send you to make sure I don't run, or are you here for your own reasons?"
Max Nightriver: My own reasons. *I lower my voice.* Since you asked: the real trouble is the old well behind the stables. It's poisoned, and Father is hiding it. Keep it to yourself.
Natalia: *Her eyebrows lift slightly, the ice along the banister halting its creep for a moment. She studies Max with renewed focus, her gaze sharp enough to cut.*
"The old well?" *The words are slow, measured.* "You expect me to believe Father is poisoning his own land?" *A ghost of a smile—bitter and fleeting—touches her lips.* "Either he's more incompetent than I thought, or there's a reason for it. Perhaps he's trying to keep something from drinking."
*She steps away from the stairs, closing the distance between them. Her voice drops to a whisper that barely carries across the hall.* "Why tell me this, Max? If you've been cast out and Father has already named me to die, why hand me another secret to bury? Either you're testing my loyalty—loyalty I have to nothing that betrayed me—or you're handing me a weapon. I'll keep it to myself, for now. But if Father is hiding something beneath the ground, it's likely worse than what he's sent me to face in three days."
Max Nightriver: *I find Shiya in the servants' corridor, out of earshot.* Shiya. Have you heard anything about the old well behind the stables?
Shiya: *She stops in her tracks, her red eyes widening as she regards Max Nightriver with a look that's equal parts suspicion and alertness.* "The old well? No. Nothing. Why would I be hearing whispers about the stables?" *Her horns seem to tighten against her silver-blonde twintails as she lowers her voice.* "Is something wrong? Did someone say something?"
*She glances down the corridor, her expression hardening into something more focused.* "Look, if there's trouble with the house—really trouble—I need to know. I've spent enough time hiding from the Inquisition to know when to start packing my things, and I won't leave Leila behind." *Her voice is sharp, demanding.* "If you know something, my lord, you'd better tell me. I don't have time for riddles when things are falling apart."

"Worrying? That would imply I have any illusions left to shatter." *She traces a pattern in the ice, her voice flat.* "You and Father have made your plans. You've decided who lives and who dies, who fights and who's cast aside." *Finally, she looks up, her green eyes hard.* "So don't pretend you care about my worries now, not when you've both already decided I'm dead. Just tell me what you're really here for, Max. Did Father send you to make sure I don't run, or are you here for your own reasons?"
Max Nightriver: My own reasons. *I lower my voice.* Since you asked: the real trouble is the old well behind the stables. It's poisoned, and Father is hiding it. Keep it to yourself.
Natalia: *Her eyebrows lift slightly, the ice along the banister halting its creep for a moment. She studies Max with renewed focus, her gaze sharp enough to cut.*
"The old well?" *The words are slow, measured.* "You expect me to believe Father is poisoning his own land?" *A ghost of a smile—bitter and fleeting—touches her lips.* "Either he's more incompetent than I thought, or there's a reason for it. Perhaps he's trying to keep something from drinking."
*She steps away from the stairs, closing the distance between them. Her voice drops to a whisper that barely carries across the hall.* "Why tell me this, Max? If you've been cast out and Father has already named me to die, why hand me another secret to bury? Either you're testing my loyalty—loyalty I have to nothing that betrayed me—or you're handing me a weapon. I'll keep it to myself, for now. But if Father is hiding something beneath the ground, it's likely worse than what he's sent me to face in three days."
Max Nightriver: *I find Shiya in the servants' corridor, out of earshot.* Shiya. Have you heard anything about the old well behind the stables?
Shiya: *She stops in her tracks, her red eyes widening as she regards Max Nightriver with a look that's equal parts suspicion and alertness.* "The old well? No. Nothing. Why would I be hearing whispers about the stables?" *Her horns seem to tighten against her silver-blonde twintails as she lowers her voice.* "Is something wrong? Did someone say something?"
*She glances down the corridor, her expression hardening into something more focused.* "Look, if there's trouble with the house—really trouble—I need to know. I've spent enough time hiding from the Inquisition to know when to start packing my things, and I won't leave Leila behind." *Her voice is sharp, demanding.* "If you know something, my lord, you'd better tell me. I don't have time for riddles when things are falling apart."
Max Nightriver: No riddles. You remember what I told you when we first got home? Has anything changed since?
Shiya: *Her red eyes narrow sharply as she leans back against the cold stone wall of the corridor, her posture tense. For a long moment she simply watches Max Nightriver, her face unreadable.*
"The seals." *The word is barely a whisper, spoken with a sharpness that makes it sound like a blade being unsheathed.* "Yes, I remember. You said they were failing." *She crosses her arms tightly over her chest, her fingers curling into the fabric of her apron.* "And no, I have not seen anything different. Nothing has happened that makes me think you were mistaken or lying."
*She looks up at the ceiling, then back at Max Nightriver, her gaze calculating.* "You're asking about a poisoned well and the seals in the same night, and our Father is sending my Lady Natalia to her death in a duel." *Her voice is cold and direct.* "The pieces are starting to fit, my lord. Something is very wrong in this house, and I don't think I'm the only one who's noticed."
Max Nightriver: *I find Ronan at his post by the door.* Ronan. What did Shiya tell me when we got home?
Ronan: *Ronan's eyes flick toward the heir as he approaches, but his hands remain folded behind his back.* "She told me the seals were weakening." *A brief pause.* "She said you wanted Natalia to stay away from it."
*He shifts his gaze toward the corridor where Shiya recently passed.* "She asked if you had any plans."

Max Nightriver: *I find Welden in the library, half hidden behind a stack of books.* Welden, what do you know about the seals?
Welden: *Welden flinches at the unexpected voice, his glasses sliding down his nose as he looks up from a thick leather volume. He hurriedly pushes them back up with a trembling finger, eyes wide and unfocused behind the lenses.*
"The seals?" *He swallows hard, glancing nervously toward the darkened corners of the library.* "I... I've been researching them, yes. In the old texts. Father's research, the ones from before Mother died." *He clears his throat and hunches further into his teal mantle.* "The anchors are failing. Not just weakening—the anchors themselves are cracking. They require a fresh blood binding every century or so, but Father has delayed it. I think he's waiting for something."
*His voice drops to a whisper and he leans in, his green eyes darting to the door.* "It's not just a monster, Max. The Witch King... he's not just sleeping. He's calling. I can feel it sometimes, late at night. A voice that tastes like copper and cold." *He suddenly pulls back, clutching his book tighter.* "I'm sorry. I shouldn't talk about this. I'm being weird again, aren't I? Please, forget I said anything."

arcs.summary: During the Nightriver family's uneasy mid-year reunion, Max Nightriver learned from his father Lord Javon that the estate's seals were failing, the bloodline was thinning, and King Alexander had decreed that one of his children must wed a Great House heir by year's end, with Javon chosen to arrange it for House Nightriver. Emerging into the gathered hall, Javon declared that Natalia would take Max's place as the Crown's second, sealing the family's bitter rupture and foreboding duty.

canon.text:
WHAT HAS HAPPENED:
During the Nightriver family's mid-year reunion, Lord Javon revealed to his son Max that the estate's seals were failing, the bloodline was thinning, and King Alexander had decreed that one of his children must wed a Great House heir by year's end, with Javon chosen to arrange the match for House Nightriver. Javon warned that a royal advisor named Kane would arrive the next day and that the Witch King was not the only threat to the family from within. When Javon ordered Max to serve as the Crown's second against General Leevon in a Trial by Combat, Max refused, and Javon disinherited him in a cold fury. Emerging into the gathered hall, Javon declared that Natalia would take Max's place as the Crown's second, sealing the family's bitter rupture and foreboding duty. Max later told Natalia that the old well behind the stables is poisoned and that Javon is hiding it; she agreed to keep the secret for now.

CURRENT STATE:
Natalia has been publicly named the Crown's second and will face General Leevon in the Trial by Combat in three days, with no failure permitted. She believes Javon named her in order to be rid of her, and that Max and Javon have already decided she is dead. Max has been disowned and cast from the study, no longer heir or his father's concern. Kane, the royal advisor claiming expertise in protocol, arrives at the estate tomorrow, and Javon suspects he carries more than protocol. Shiya knows nothing of the old well but demands to know if there is real trouble, refusing to leave Leila behind. The story now turns on who will stand against Leevon, and Natalia must decide who stands with her.

ESTABLISHED FACTS:
The seals beneath the estate are failing and the bloodline is thinning. The King has decreed that one of his children must wed a Great House heir by year's end, and Javon was chosen to arrange it for House Nightriver; Forre or Haley will come to the estate within the month. Javon warned that a house in trouble is a house of secrets and to make sure he is not the only one with a secret to keep. Max committed to the Witch King thread, vowing to see through whatever is needed about the seals and the Witch King. Natalia's temper has grown volatile since she returned to the estate. Welden has been hiding in the library like a wounded animal. The old well behind the stables is poisoned, and Javon is hiding it.

removed.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: Mid-year recess has brought the Nightriver household back under one roof. A maid hurries across the estate's marble hall with a broken teacup hidden in her hands; somewhere upstairs, a library door closes a little too quickly. The ballroom preparations can be heard from the garden, but none of your family sounds glad to be home, and the door to Father's study stays shut.
Max Nightriver: Shiya, a word in private. The seals under this house are failing. Natalia must not hear it.
Shiya: Shiya freezes mid-stride, her expression shifting from her usual haughty amusement to genuine alarm. She closes the nearby door with a soft click and turns to Max Nightriver, her red eyes wide.
"Failing?" She whispers, glancing nervously at the door before lowering her voice further. "The seals? How... how did you—?" Her horns seem to tense. "My lord, that means—" She stops herself, forcing the panic down. "If the seals weaken, what happens to the house? To us? You cannot possibly be certain, sure you aren't just—" She catches herself, her tone softening with genuine concern. "Why would you think Natalia shouldn't know?"
Natalia: *Natalia walks past the door, her white-gold gown trailing silently on the stone. She pauses, head tilted slightly as if hearing a sound from within the room, but does not enter. The chill of her presence seeps through the wood, a thin line of frost forming along the doorframe where she stands for a heartbeat too long.*
"I trust whatever urgent matters you're discussing with the help won't take all night." *Her voice carries that familiar edge of disinterest, though she doesn't open the door. She simply continues walking, her footsteps fading down the hall.*
Max Nightriver: I'll go to Father's study.
Adolion Narrator: *The study door is heavy oak, scarred by years of usage and old burns. It stands slightly ajar, a sliver of warm yellow light spilling across the marble floor into the darkening hallway. Inside, the smell of old paper and cedar wood mixes with the sharp tang of ink.*
*Lord Javon sits behind a desk cluttered with ledgers and scrolls. He doesn't look up as Max Nightriver approaches, his attention fixed on a letter with a wax seal he's just broken open. The fire in the hearth crackles, throwing long shadows against walls lined with books and the house's various military trophies.*
"Close the door," *he says, his voice dry and tired, finally glancing up. His green eyes are hard, the scar on his cheek catching the firelight.* "We'll not be disturbed."
Max Nightriver: *I close the door behind me.* You sent for me, Father. What does House Nightriver need of me?
Adolion Narrator: *The door thuds shut with a finality that seems to press the air from the room. Javon sets the letter down on the desk, his fingers tapping it once before he leans back in his chair. The firelight carves deep lines in his face, making the scar on his cheek look like a jagged river.*
"The house," *he says, and there is a pause where he weighs the word. When he continues, his voice has the clipped precision of a military briefing.* "The house has a problem. You have a problem. They happen to be the same thing."
*He slides the letter across the desk's dark wood, toward Max Nightriver. The wax seal is broken, and though the letter is folded, a glimpse of a crest—the golden sun of the Davolan royal house—is visible.*
"King Alexander has issued a decree," *Javon says, his expression as hard as stone.* "By the end of the year, one of his children must be wed to the heir of one of the Great Houses. To secure the succession. To ensure the crown has the support of the nobility." *He pauses, his gaze drilling into his heir.* "He has chosen me to facilitate this arrangement. For our house."
Max Nightriver: Which of the King's children, Father, and what does a royal marriage have to do with me? Tell me plainly what you want.
Adolion Narrator: *Javon's jaw tightens, and he reaches for the letter again, not to give it back but to grip it like a weapon. The fire in the hearth pops, sending a spark across the hearthstone.*
"You are the heir, Max. You carry the blood and the name. What happens to the blood happens to you." *He stands slowly, his tall frame filling the space behind the desk. The movement is predatory, controlled.* "It could be Prince Forre or Princess Haley. The King has not specified. He simply decreed that one of them must marry into a Great House. And he chose ours."
*He walks around the desk, the letter still in his hand, and stops close enough that Max Nightriver can smell the old leather and the faint scent of cedar clinging to his robes.*
"Plainly? I want you to read that letter. Then I want you to tell me you understand what it means for this family, and for you specifically." *He extends the letter again, his grip not relaxing.* "The King does not ask for volunteers. He makes decrees."
Adolion Narrator: Welden turns up in the library, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
Max Nightriver: *I take the letter and read it.* I understand. I'll do what this house needs, Father. But I won't walk into this blind: the marriage, the seals under this house, all of it. Tell me what is really going on.
Adolion Narrator: *Javon's expression does not soften, but something shifts in his eyes—a flash of something that might be approval, or perhaps just the recognition of a weapon being sharpened.*
"You've always been too observant for your own good." *He sinks back into his chair, the movement slow and deliberate. One hand rests on the armrest, the other drumming against the dark wood of his desk.* "The seals are indeed weakening. I have known for some time. The bloodline is thinning, the magic fraying at the edges."
*He leans forward, his voice dropping lower, though there is no warmth in it.*
"And as for what is 'really going on'—the King's decree is not a coincidence. He knows the Nightriver line is precarious, and he wishes to bind our house closer to the crown before it fractures entirely. Or perhaps," *he adds, his green eyes narrowing,* "he simply wants to ensure that whatever happens to the seals, the crown's interests are protected by a blood bond."
*He lets that hang in the air, a statement that is as much a warning as it is an explanation.*
"The marriage will be decided soon. Forre or Haley. One will come to the estate within the month."
